description: SQL Server engine health from windows_exporter: buffer pool (PLE, cache hit), blocking, batch/compile rates, log space, memory grants and lock/wait pressure.

panels.description: SQL sub-collector failures. Non-zero means these numbers are stale - check the exporter service account permissions.
panels.title: MSSQL Scrape FAIL

panels.description: Instances with blocked processes. Every blocked session is a user waiting - find the head blocker first.
panels.title: Blocking Now

panels.description: Page Life Expectancy below 300s means the buffer pool is being churned - pages are evicted before they are reused.
panels.title: PLE < 300s

panels.description: Queries waiting for memory (RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE). Users see this as a hang, not as slowness.
panels.title: Pending Grants

panels.description: Worst buffer pool in the selection.
panels.title: Min PLE

panels.description: Fullest transaction log. At 100% all writes to that database stop.
panels.title: Max Log Used %

panels.description: Busiest instance by batch requests per second - your throughput baseline.
panels.title: Max Batch/s

panels.description: User connections across all selected instances.
panels.title: Total Connections

panels.description: Any sustained deadlock rate needs an application or index fix, not a server fix.
panels.title: Deadlocks/s

panels.description: A long-running transaction holds locks and prevents log truncation.
panels.title: Longest Txn

panels.description: Memory pressure ranking - start here for "SQL is slow" reports.
panels.title: Lowest PLE (bottomk 15)

panels.description: Busiest instances by workload.
panels.title: Highest Batch Requests/s (topk 15)

panels.description: Log space ranking. Check backup jobs and open transactions on anything above 80%.
panels.title: Highest Log Used % (topk 15)

panels.description: One row per SQL instance. High Page Reads/s with low PLE and low Cache Hit % is the classic "needs more RAM or better indexes" signature.
panels.title: SQL Health by Instance

panels.description: Free list stalls confirm real buffer pool starvation rather than a transient PLE dip after a large scan.

targets.expr: label_join((max by(instance,mssql_instance) (windows_mssql_genstats_blocked_processes{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"})) and on(instance,mssql_instance) ((min by(instance,mssql_instance) (windows_mssql_bufman_page_life_expectancy_seconds{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"})) < 600 or (max by(instance,mssql_instance) (windows_mssql_genstats_blocked_processes{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"})) > 0), "hv", " | ", "instance", "mssql_instance")

label_join((sum by(instance,mssql_instance) (rate(windows_mssql_bufman_page_reads{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"}[5m]))) and on(instance,mssql_instance) ((min by(instance,mssql_instance) (windows_mssql_bufman_page_life_expectancy_seconds{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"})) < 600 or (max by(instance,mssql_instance) (windows_mssql_genstats_blocked_processes{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"})) > 0), "hv", " | ", "instance", "mssql_instance")

label_join((sum by(instance,mssql_instance) (rate(windows_mssql_bufman_free_list_stalls{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"}[5m]))) and on(instance,mssql_instance) ((min by(instance,mssql_instance) (windows_mssql_bufman_page_life_expectancy_seconds{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"})) < 600 or (max by(instance,mssql_instance) (windows_mssql_genstats_blocked_processes{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}"})) > 0), "hv", " | ", "instance", "mssql_instance")

panels.title: Hotspots: PLE < 600s or Blocking

panels.description: Per-database log pressure. Usual causes: missing log backup, an open transaction, or replication / AG not draining.
panels.title: Hotspot: Transaction Log > 80% Used

panels.description: A sawtooth that resets to near zero means the buffer pool is being flushed - look for large scans or a restart. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Page Life Expectancy (bottomk 10)

panels.description: Workload volume. Compare shape with CPU on Collector cpu to separate more work from slower work.
panels.title: Batch Requests/s (topk 10)

panels.description: Any non-zero plateau is an active blocking chain. The width of the plateau is how long users waited.
panels.title: Blocked Processes (topk 10)

panels.description: Healthy pattern is a sawtooth that drops at each log backup. A flat climb means truncation is blocked.
panels.title: Transaction Log Used % (topk 10)

panels.description: Total at Target means SQL has taken all the memory it is allowed. Below target means it does not need more yet.
panels.title: Server Memory vs Target (topk 10)

panels.description: Below ~98% on an OLTP instance means reads are going to disk. Read it together with PLE, never alone.
panels.title: Buffer Cache Hit % (bottomk 10)

panels.description: Compiles above ~10% of batch requests means poor plan reuse - look for unparameterised ad-hoc SQL.
panels.title: Compilations / Recompilations per second (topk 10)

panels.description: Rising lock waits precede timeouts and deadlocks. Fix the index or the transaction scope, not the timeout setting.
panels.title: Lock Waits / Timeouts / Deadlocks per second (topk 10)

panels.description: Page splits indicate fill-factor or index-key problems; full scans indicate missing indexes.
panels.title: Access Methods: Page Splits & Full Scans per second (topk 10)

panels.description: Both rising together is unambiguous buffer pool pressure.
panels.title: Free List Stalls & Lazy Writes per second (topk 10)

panels.description: Pending grants above zero means queries are queued on RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE and users are waiting.
panels.title: Memory Grants & Active Transactions (topk 10)

panels.description: Which wait class dominates tells you where to spend effort: page IO latch = storage or memory, log write = log disk, network IO = client side.
panels.title: Wait Statistics & Errors

panels.description: FAIL rows mean every metric on this dashboard is stale for that host. Fix the exporter first, then re-read the KPIs.
panels.title: Scrape Health by Host

panels.description: Growing duration usually means the host is under load or the collector is querying more objects. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Scrape Duration (topk 10)

panels.description: Dips to 0 mark scrape gaps. Correlate with the flat spots you see in the trend panels above.
panels.title: Scrape Success (bottomk 10)
